```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "Idea B has in-category price evidence. Since.dev lists a $149/mo Studio tier and Nalvis lists a hosted tier from $14/mo. Idea A has no competitor that charges anything: all five live competitors are free or donation-supported, and its price anchor comes from a different category (GPTZero AI-text detection).",
    "Idea A's strongest market signal is negative. Fakespot, well funded and well distributed, shut down in July 2025 rather than sustain itself. Idea A's own brief treats this as evidence that the category struggles to monetize even at scale.",
    "Idea B's payer is a business (engineering leads at startups and SMBs) with a concrete, costly failure mode. Its demand quotes describe production breakage, user complaints and billing failures. Idea A's payer is a consumer asked to pay for something already available free on the same store listings.",
    "Idea B's demand quotes come from developers describing incidents that hit them. Two of Idea A's three quotes are builder launch threads ('I created a script to spot AI bots'). Idea A's third quote is an explicit counter-signal calling such detectors 'downright immoral'.",
    "Both ideas face crowded fields and free open-source competitors, so density does not separate them. What separates them is that Idea B's field shows willingness to charge, and Idea A's shows none. That makes B the better bet for a first paying customer within 90 days.",
    "Idea B carries real risk that is not waved away here. Its own brief says teams may not grant PR/write access without security vetting that a solo operator cannot credibly establish in six weeks. Its first customer likely has to be a small, low-bureaucracy team, possibly using a read-only or local-only scan."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea A's price hypothesis is the weakest evidence. Its anchor of 'typical consumer extension subscriptions (~$4.99/month)' has no source and so counts as missing. Its only sourced anchor, GPTZero at $10-15/month, is a different product category. No competitor in the actual category charges at all, so nothing supports the claim that a reader would pay $3-5/month.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. Neither brief shows a single confirmed paying customer. Idea B's price anchors are also soft: Nalvis is pre-launch/waitlist, Since.dev's Pro price is undisclosed, and mendapi's hosted tier has no price. Several of Idea B's case-against claims carry no citation, including vendors like Stripe building native tooling and SOC 2 being commonly expected, so they count as missing. However, the security-trust barrier to code access is Idea B's own stated main obstacle and could plausibly block a sale within 90 days. B wins mainly because Idea A's evidence points actively against monetization, not because Idea B's evidence is strong."
}
```
